full_judgment: 3. Mr. Md. Moksudur Rahman submits that the payment to the national exchequer was , made under the order of the Government and the payment not being out of the volitin of the assessee-company, the same, does not attract, clause,(XVI) of sub-section (2) of Section, 10 of the Act. He continues to any that unless the expenditure is spent for the purpose, of carrying out of the business of the assessee-company out of its own volition, the expenses incurred is not a deductible allowance within the meaning of Section 10(2)(XVI) of the Act. He further submits that in order to attract this provision of law the assessee must show that the expenses incurred was wholly and exclusively for the purpose of the business. He also submits that the order of the Tribunal does not indicate that at what stage the payment to the national exchequer was made. In other words, he submits that whether the payment is a diversion of income'' before it reached or accrued to the assessee-company or out of the profits and unless no such finding is arrived at by the tribunal. Its order directing deletion of the amount from computing total income cannot be held legal. He refers us to the decision of Sitaldas Tirathdas to contend that in that case the payment to the wife and children ‘of the assessee pursuant to a decree of Court was held not to be a deductible allowance claimed by the assessee. The payment there was made out of the income of the assessee himself. Therefore on decision does not help the Revenue as we find the Tribunal, on facts held that the payments to the national exchequer were paid wholly and exclusive by the assessee for the purpose of its business. The aforesaid finding Of the Tribunal indicates that the payment was diversion of income before it reached or Secure to the assessee. Where a payment is a diversion of income before the same reaches the hands of the assessee satisfies the requirements of clause XVI of Sub-section (2) of Section 10 provided that payment is made wholly and exclusively for the purpose of carrying on the business of the assessee. As, in this case, the Tribunal found on facts that the payment was made for the purpose of the business of the assessee, we hold that the payment qualifies deduction U/S 10(2) (XVI) of the Act.
